outcome_variable_scope: Own-minus-donor accuracy against a THIRD of each pair's human raters, divided by that label's measured reliability, binned by a disjoint third's consensus. Satisfaction from r04's tensor; no new measurement and no new judge call.
scope: The correction assumes arm errors are independent of label errors; correlated errors bias the corrected curve toward flatness, so a surviving rise is robust and a flat result is not. Accuracy LEVELS are not comparable to r103's, which labelled with all raters; only the gradient is. Pairs under 9 raters are excluded because a three-way split needs a majority in each third, and every pair is subsampled to exactly 12 so that label size is constant across bins.
verdict: S SPECIFICITY. r103 found source specificity rising from +0.0283 to +0.2461 across human-consensus bins and named its own residual: a noisy target attenuates every estimator toward chance, so the rise is expected even under constant specificity. Attenuation is MEASURABLE. Splitting each pair's raters in THREE -- one third supplies the scoring label, one third measures that label's reliability, one third does the binning, so the binning variable touches neither -- EVERY pair is subsampled to a fixed pool of 12 raters, so |A|=|B|=|C|=4 in every bin and the bins differ in consensus and nothing else -- the first version let the third size vary, which made the bins a RATER-COUNT partition and showed up as the lowest-consensus bin carrying the MOST reliable label. Ties in a third are broken at random rather than dropped, since dropping them conditions on the label being decisive. The two probe thirds agree 0.652, 0.735, 0.865 across bins, giving attenuation factors 0.552, 0.685, 0.855. Dividing each arm's over-chance accuracy by its bin's factor, the attribution runs +0.1546, +0.2038, +0.2491 against a raw +0.0853, +0.1396, +0.2128. The low-to-high rise falls from +0.1276 raw to +0.0945 corrected, 26% of it removed, 95% CI over PAIRS [+0.0607,+0.1281]. THE GRADIENT SURVIVES ITS OWN NOISE MODEL: the rubric resolves consensual comparisons better than contested ones even after the label's unreliability is divided out. That is the reverse of what a normative instrument should do -- contested pairs are where prompt-specific values would earn their keep, and the measured specificity is concentrated where it matters least. BOTH ARMS RISE AFTER CORRECTION, AND THAT IS A SECOND READING OF THE SAME TABLE: the own arm's deattenuated accuracy runs 0.7225 to 0.8641 and the DONOR arm's runs 0.5679 to 0.6151. Under the independent-noise model a constant-accuracy arm is FLAT after correction -- the simulation control shows exactly that -- so NEITHER arm is constant. An UNRELATED rubric also resolves consensual pairs better than contested ones, which is a general normative backbone behaving as one would expect of it. The attribution's rise is the EXCESS of the own arm's rise over the donor's, and it is that excess, not either level, that this round reports. TWO-SIDED SIMULATION CONTROL, both required and both passed: synthetic raters with a per-pair agreement probability spanning the bins and an arm of CONSTANT latent accuracy 0.750 produce a rising raw curve that the correction flattens to +0.0002, recovering the planted value to 0.025; an arm whose latent accuracy genuinely RISES keeps a corrected rise of +0.1110. An instrument that flattened everything would report the first world whatever the truth, so the second control is the one that makes a flat result mean anything. THE CONFOUND, WRITTEN BEFORE THE RUN AND NOT SOFTENED: the correction assumes the arm's errors are INDEPENDENT of the label's. A rubric and a rater can be misled by the same surface feature, plausibly more often on contested pairs, and positively correlated errors make the correction UNDER-correct where correlation is high -- biasing this round's corrected curve UPWARD at the low end, i.e. TOWARD flatness. So a surviving rise is the robust finding here and a flat one is the result this design could manufacture. A SECOND EFFECT PUSHES THE SAME WAY: the binning third holds only 4 raters, so its consensus is a noisy estimate of the underlying rater agreement and the bins are smeared into one another. Smearing pulls every bin toward the pooled mean and SHRINKS the measured gradient, so the corrected rise is a LOWER BOUND rather than an estimate. REPRODUCIBILITY, AND IT WAS NOT FREE: pairs were first collected by iterating a set, whose order depends on python's per-process string hashing, so the pair indices and every split drawn from the seeded generator differed run to run -- four runs of the unchanged file gave corrected rises of +0.0968, +0.1179, +0.1056 and +0.1114. Every seed in the file was correct and the round was still not seeded. The set is now sorted and the figures below are stable under PYTHONHASHSEED. SCOPE: 3,929 unordered pairs carrying at least 12 raters, 12 random three-way splits each; the bootstrap resamples PAIRS, since one pair contributing 12 rows is not 12 pieces of evidence. The label here is a THIRD of the raters, not all of them, so these accuracies are not comparable to r103's levels -- only their gradient is.
